Class ViewMyLessons

java.lang.Object
guiMyLessons.ViewMyLessons
public class ViewMyLessons extends Object

Title: ViewMyLessons Class.

Description: The Java/FX-based My Lessons Page. It shows the logged-in contributor a list of the lessons learned that contributor has added (Contributor story 2), including any a curator has since edited (Contributor story 4), and nothing added by other contributors. Each lesson shows its title and category, plus a "Locked" tag when a curator has locked the lesson or any of its fields and an "Edited by curator" tag when a curator has edited it. The contributor can search their lessons by keyword, open one to examine it more closely, or go to the Add Lesson page.

The layout follows the team's User Experience document: a light background, a small breadcrumb above a bold page title, related widgets grouped in a bordered card with labels above the fields, a blue button for the main action, and a bottom row of plain buttons for leaving the page. This page is the template the other contributor pages copy for that styling.

  • Constructor Details

    • ViewMyLessons

      private ViewMyLessons()

      Method: ViewMyLessons()

      Description: This method initializes all the elements of the graphical user interface. This method determines the location, size, font, color, and change and event handlers for each GUI object.

      This is a singleton and is only performed once. Subsequent uses fill in the changeable fields using the displayMyLessons method.

  • Method Details

    • displayMyLessons

      public static void displayMyLessons(javafx.stage.Stage ps, entityClasses.User user)

      Method: displayMyLessons(Stage ps, User user)

      Description: This method is the single entry point from outside this package to cause the My Lessons page to be displayed. It first sets up every shared attribute so we don't have to pass parameters. It then checks to see if the page has been setup. If not, it instantiates the class, initializes all the static aspects of the GUI widgets (e.g., location on the page, font, size, and any methods to be performed). After the instantiation, the code clears any earlier search and loads this contributor's lessons from the database. The page is a singleton, so this matters: a different contributor may have used the page before, and their lessons and search must not remain. It then sets the Scene onto the stage, and makes it visible to the user.

      Parameters:
      ps - specifies the JavaFX Stage to be used for this GUI and it's methods
      user - specifies the User for this GUI and it's methods

    • displayMyLessons

      public static void displayMyLessons(javafx.stage.Stage ps, entityClasses.User user, String message)

      Method: displayMyLessons(Stage ps, User user, String message)

      Description: Displays the page with a confirmation message, such as "Lesson added." after the Add Lesson page saves a lesson or "Lesson deleted." after the Lesson Detail page deletes one. The message tells the contributor the action worked, since the page that performed it is no longer showing.

      Parameters:
      ps - specifies the JavaFX Stage to be used for this GUI and it's methods
      user - specifies the User for this GUI and it's methods
      message - specifies the confirmation to show (shown in green)

    • displayMyLessons

      public static void displayMyLessons(javafx.stage.Stage ps, entityClasses.User user, String message, boolean isError)

      Method: displayMyLessons(Stage ps, User user, String message, boolean isError)

      Description: Displays the page with a message in green for a confirmation or red for an error, such as the not-found message when a selected lesson no longer exists. The other two display methods call this one, so the page is always set up the same way.

      Parameters:
      ps - specifies the JavaFX Stage to be used for this GUI and it's methods
      user - specifies the User for this GUI and it's methods
      message - specifies the message to show ("" for none)
      isError - true to show the message as an error
